topics.name: Sum of the first n terms

questions.title: Three consecutive terms: find x
questions.text: The value of x for which 2x, (x + 10) and (3x + 2) are the three consecutive terms of an A.P., is ______.
steps: ① In an A.P. the middle term is the average of its neighbours
questions.remember:
a, b, c are in A.P. ⟺ 2b = a + c.
The middle term is the average of its neighbours.
questions.trap: Writing (x + 10) − 2x = (3x + 2) − 2x. Subtract each term from the NEXT one.
questions.tryit: For what k are k + 2, 4k − 6 and 3k − 2 consecutive terms of an A.P.?

questions.title: Which term is 16?
questions.text: Which term of the A.P. −29, −26, −23, ....., 61 is 16?
questions.remember:
aₙ = a + (n − 1)d
n − 1 = number of jumps from the first term.
questions.trap: Stopping at n − 1 = 15 and picking 15th. Add the first term back: n = 16.
questions.tryit: Which term of the A.P. 3, 8, 13, 18, … is 78?

questions.title: nth term with fractions
questions.text: The nth term of the A.P. −1/3, 2/3, 5/3, 8/3, ......, is:
questions.remember:
aₙ = a + (n − 1)d
Check your formula by putting n = 1.
questions.trap: Picking (n − 4)/3. Put n = 1: it gives −1, not −1/3.
questions.tryit: Find the nth term of the A.P. 3/2, 1/2, −1/2, …

questions.title: Assertion–Reason: 2b = a + c and odd numbers
questions.text:
Assertion (A): a, b, c are in A.P. if and only if 2b = a + c.
Reason (R): The sum of first n odd natural numbers is n².
opts: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
steps: ① A: equal jumps: b − a = c − b ⟺ 2b = a + c  ✓ true
④ A is about 3 terms; R is about a SUM
⑤ R does NOT explain A
questions.remember:
1 + 3 + 5 + … + (2n − 1) = n²
Both true ≠ option (a). Ask: does R give the REASON for A?
questions.trap: Picking (a) just because both statements are true.
questions.tryit: Find the sum of the first 15 odd natural numbers.

questions.title: From 32 down to −10
questions.text: In an A.P., the first term is 32 and the last term is −10. If the common difference is −2, then find the number of terms and their sum.
questions.remember: Know the last term? Use Sₙ = n/2 (a + l). It's the fastest.
questions.trap: Writing (n − 1)(−2) = 42. From 32 to −10 is a DROP: −42.
questions.tryit: Find the sum of the A.P. 7, 10.5, 14, …, 84.

questions.title: Sum of 20 terms when aₙ = 5 − 2n
questions.text: Find the sum of first 20 terms of an A.P. whose nth term is given as aₙ = 5 – 2n.
steps: ① First term: put n = 1 ⟹ a₁ = 5 − 2 = 3
questions.remember:
Given aₙ? Put n = 1 for a, and n = 20 for the last term.
d = coefficient of n (here −2).
questions.trap: Taking a = 5. The first term is a₁ = 5 − 2 = 3.
questions.tryit: Find the sum of the first 28 terms of the A.P. with aₙ = 3n − 2. (CBSE 2026)

questions.title: Sₘ = Sₙ ⟹ Sₘ₊ₙ = 0
questions.text: If the sum of first m terms of an A.P. is same as sum of its first n terms (m ≠ n), then show that the sum of its first (m + n) terms is zero.
steps: ② × 2, group: 2a(m − n) + d[(m² − n²) − (m − n)] = 0
questions.remember: m² − n² = (m − n)(m + n). Look for (m − n) to take common.
questions.trap: Dividing by (m − n) without saying m ≠ n. Write it: that line carries a mark.
questions.tryit: If S₁₀ = S₁₅ for an A.P., find S₂₅.

questions.title: Ridhi's polygon: angles 8°, 12°, 16°, …
questions.text: Ridhi drew a polygon with n sides. The smallest exterior angle is 8° and each subsequent exterior angle is 4° more than the previous exterior angle. Find the number of sides of the polygon that Ridhi had drawn.
steps: ① Exterior angles of ANY polygon add up to 360°
questions.remember: The exterior angles of ANY polygon add up to 360°.
questions.trap: Using 180° or (n − 2) × 180°. Those are for interior angles.
questions.tryit: How many terms of 9, 17, 25, … give a sum of 636?

questions.title: a + a₈ = 32, a × a₈ = 60 (5 marks)
questions.text: The sum of first and eighth terms of an A.P. is 32 and their product is 60. Find the first term and common difference of the A.P. Hence, also find the sum of its first 20 terms.
questions.remember: Sum and product of two numbers given? They are the roots of t² − (sum)t + product = 0.
questions.trap: Giving only one case. a = 30, d = −4 also fits, and it carries marks.
questions.tryit: The 4th term of an A.P. is 0. Prove that its 25th term is triple its 11th term.

questions.title: Case study: the car loan
questions.text:
Your elder brother wants to buy a car and plans to take a loan from a bank for his car. He repays his total loan of ₹ 1,18,000 by paying every month, starting with the first instalment of ₹ 1,000 and he increases the instalment by ₹ 100 every month.
(i) Find the amount paid by him in the 30th instalment.  (ii) If the total number of instalments is 40, what is the amount paid in the last instalment?  (iii) What amount does he still have to pay after the 30th instalment? [OR Find the ratio of the tenth instalment to the last instalment.]
questions.remember: Amount in ONE instalment ⟹ aₙ.  Total paid so far ⟹ Sₙ.
questions.trap: Using a₃₀ for the amount already paid. 'Paid so far' is a SUM: S₃₀.
questions.tryit: Check: do 40 instalments really add up to ₹ 1,18,000?
